svg.title: Honcho: a reasoner that works in the background
svg.desc: Honcho's architecture, with the running example. Writing: when messages arrive, a deriver makes one LLM call per batch that extracts what was said as explicit conclusions; later, a dream runs two agents with tools that add deductive and inductive conclusions, delete outdated ones and keep a peer card. Memory: conclusions at levels, each derived one citing the conclusions it was drawn from; the contradiction level has no writer in this release. In the run shown, the vegetarian fact was deleted, but a deduction and a pattern that rest on it stayed live. Reading: either Honcho's dialectic agent writes an answer from the conclusions (an LLM call), or the representation returns the conclusions themselves, with their times (no LLM call). The dialectic's prefetch held both the update and the stale conclusions; its answer said pescatarian and kept all four constraints.
